newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt to phase out lead in petrol.
newsitem.headline: Egypt to phase out lead in petrol.

text.p: Egypt will try to phase out tetraethyl lead as a fuel additive by the middle of 1997 for environmental reasons, government newspapers said on Thursday.

A cabinet meeting on Wednesday agreed to an Oil Ministry proposal to stop selling leaded fuel first in Greater Cairo, Alexandria, the three Suez Canal towns, the north coast, Sinai and the Red Sea area, they said.
"Efforts will continue to cover all parts of the country by the middle of 1997," said the government newspaper al-Ahram, quoting government spokesman Safwat el-Sherif.
Unleaded fuel has already gone on sale at several service stations in Cairo but very few vehicles have been modified to use it in place of leaded fuel.
Oil Ministry officials were not available on Thursday to explain the timetable for the switch or what arrangements would be made to adjust engines.
The Egyptian government was a late convert to the campaign against lead, a major pollutant in Cairo, but it is now trying to catch up.
World Bank experts say lead levels in Cairo air and in the blood of many Cairo residents exceeds the maximum recommended by the World Health Organisation.

Among Cairo children, lead levels in the blood varies from 13 to 25 micrograms per decilitre, while in traffic policemen the level can be 60 micrograms. Ten micrograms per decilitre is a widely accepted maximum level.
Most comes from vehicles but lead smelters in populated areas also contribute. The government says it is moving the smelters to industrial estates in the desert.
